channel.title: Cadence 步频 — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 50 sources.

item.title: Clinical practice guideline for physical therapist management of total knee arthroplasty: revision 2026.
item.description: The American Physical Therapy Association has released a 2026 revision of its clinical practice guideline for physical therapist management of total knee arthroplasty, updating the 2020 version based on a systematic review of current literature and formulating 20 recommendations.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Physical and mental health-related quality of life outcomes of non-pharmacological interventions in early multiple sclerosis: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis found effects of non-pharmacological interventions on physical and mental health-related quality of life among adults with early diagnosed multiple sclerosis, with findings pooled using standardized mean differences.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Exercise Interventions for Older Adults with Alzheimer's Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 142 articles explored the effectiveness of physical exercise on cognitive function and optimal dosage in older adults with Alzheimer's disease, drawing from Embase, PsycInfo, and Ovid Medline databases.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Fee Schedules - General Information
item.description: The CMS "Fee Schedules - General Information" outlines the complete listing of fees Medicare uses to pay doctors and other providers/suppliers, including ambulance, clinical laboratory, DMEPOS, and physician fee schedules.
item.author: CMS

item.title: Outcomes of rehabilitation following device-aided therapy start in parkinson's disease: a randomized controlled trial.
item.description: An open-label randomized controlled trial with 45 completers found that adding 3 months of tailored primary care rehabilitation to device-aided therapy in Parkinson's disease patients resulted in better maintenance of patient motor skills at 6 and 12 months.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: External Validation of a Machine Learning Model for the Early Prediction of Upper-Limb Recovery After Stroke.
item.description: This study externally validated a machine learning model for predicting 6-month upper-limb capacity after stroke (ARAT scores) using an independent Danish prospective cohort, following development on a multicenter Dutch cohort of first-ever ischemic stroke patients.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effectiveness of an AI-based home exercise app for rehabilitation of rotator cuff-related shoulder pain: A randomized controlled trial.
item.description: A single-center RCT (N=46) found that adding an AI-based digital rehabilitation program with real-time computer vision feedback to standard physiotherapy significantly improved pain and function in adults with rotator cuff-related shoulder pain over 12 weeks.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Additive Effects of Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation and Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation on Robotic Therapy for Upper Extremity Recovery After Chronic Ischemic Stroke: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Sham-Controlled Trial.
item.description: A randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial (N=36) in chronic ischemic stroke patients found that adding repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) or transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) to robotic therapy did not provide additional benefits for upper extremity motor and functional recovery.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Remotely Monitored Home-based Pulmonary Rehabilitation in Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis: Results of a Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (N=29) in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) on antifibrotic therapy demonstrated that a 12-week asynchronously remotely monitored, exercise-focused home pulmonary rehabilitation program was feasible and effective.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation for Dizziness, Balance, and Postural Stability in Adult Patients With Chronic Peripheral Vestibular Dizziness.
item.description: A double-blind RCT of 56 adults with chronic vestibular dizziness found that 8 weeks of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) combined with vestibular rehabilitation (VR) significantly improved dizziness, balance, and postural stability compared to sham rTMS plus VR.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Bidirectional association between injuries and mental health symptoms among elite athletes: a systematic review
item.description: A systematic review of 25 studies found a bidirectional association between musculoskeletal injuries and mental health symptoms among elite athletes, indicating that mental health symptoms can precede injury, and injury can lead to subsequent mental health symptoms.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Clinically interpretable prediction models of stroke functional outcomes: A national cohort study of adults in inpatient rehabilitation facilities in the US.
item.description: A retrospective cohort study (n=43,745) developed clinically interpretable prediction models for self-care and mobility function at discharge from US inpatient rehabilitation facilities for adults with stroke, using only Inpatient Rehabilitation Facility Patient Assessment Instrument (IRF-PAI) variables.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effect of kinesiology taping on limb oedema in patients with severe hyper-dependency using shear-wave elastography: a randomized clinical trial.
item.description: A randomized clinical trial (n=50) demonstrated that kinesiology taping at 25% tension significantly reduced the elastic coefficient of the dermis in patients with limb oedema compared to 0% tension taping by day 9, with effects sustained to day 16.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Virtual reality-assisted rehabilitation after arthroscopic rotator cuff repair for small-to-medium supraspinatus tears: a prospective assessor-blinded randomized controlled trial
item.description: A prospective assessor-blinded randomized controlled trial examined virtual reality-assisted rehabilitation after arthroscopic rotator cuff repair for small-to-medium supraspinatus tears, noting VR's potential to standardize tasks and provide feedback.
item.author: BMC Musculoskelet Disord

item.title: Slow eccentric- versus concentric-focused resistance training in middle-aged and older women with knee osteoarthritis: A randomized trial
item.description: A randomized trial compared the short-term effects of slow eccentric-only resistance training (SET) and slow concentric-only resistance training (SCT) on pain and physical function in middle-aged and older women with knee osteoarthritis.
item.author: BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil

item.title: Nordic walking and sprinting enhance lower limb vertical power in Parkinson’s: an exploratory study
item.description: An exploratory study found that Nordic walking and sprinting enhanced lower limb vertical power, specifically jump height and peak power, in individuals with Parkinson's disease.
item.author: Sport Sci Health

item.title: Biopsychosocial predictors of functional recovery in chronic low back pain following physiotherapy: A survival analysis study.
item.description: A prospective observational cohort study of 250 adults with chronic non-specific low back pain found that baseline biopsychosocial factors, particularly Oswestry Disability Index (ODI) and pain catastrophizing, predicted functional recovery time following individualized physiotherapy.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Applying the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health to Classify Upper Limb Outcome Measures in Stroke Rehabilitation: A Construct-Driven Perspective.
item.description: This perspective emphasizes using the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) to classify upper limb outcome measures in stroke rehabilitation, advocating for a construct-driven approach to clarify whether measures assess neuromuscular impairments or activity limitations.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: The effect of online physical activity monitoring on physical activity level, psychological health, fatigue, and quality of life in patients with multiple sclerosis: a randomized controlled trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial with 42 individuals with multiple sclerosis (MS) found that continuous online monitoring of walking-based physical activity via a messaging application significantly improved physical activity levels, psychological health, and quality of life.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Depressive symptoms in high-performance athletes and non-athletes: a comparative meta-analysis update
item.description: An updated comparative meta-analysis of 10 studies found no significant difference in the prevalence of mild or more severe depressive symptoms between high-performance athletes and non-athletes.
item.author: BJSM
